title: prefill-cache-coalescing-weekly-notes-2026-04-12
content:
Weekly notes — prefill cache + coalescing experiments (wk of 2026-04-12)
Owner: Aditi Rao (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Marcus Li, Sofia Alvarez, Ethan Park
Status: draft — working notes, perf numbers provisional

Purpose
- Capture the outcomes from this week's kernel + KV cache work and batching/coalescing experiments.
- Surface regressions, next experiments, and roll-forward/rollback criteria for canary.

Quick summary / highlights
- Prefill-based cache hits: end-to-end p99 reduced from 270ms -> 190ms on short-chat traces when prefill hit rate > 45%.
- Coalescing strategy (early coalesce window 8ms) reduced RPC overhead for small concurrent requests by ~18% token/sec improvement for low-latency tier.
- Kernel patch r879 (see PR) landed basic fused-gemm changes; 3% throughput uplift in 2k token tests but introduced a non-deterministic OOM on some long-sequence (>12k tokens) repro cases. Patch reverted on canary infra until OOM root cause fixed.
- Action items: add deterministic reproduction test, add guarded allocation, and extend CI mem-pressure runner.

Benchmarks and numbers (lab cluster: p4d-24, model: rw-3B-quantized-v2, test harness: local-sim)
- Baseline (no prefill, batch size auto): mean latency 85ms, p95 210ms, p99 270ms, tokens/sec 1420
- Prefill-enabled (cache hit path): mean latency 70ms, p95 160ms, p99 190ms, tokens/sec 1680 (hit rate 47%)
- Coalescing enabled (8ms window) + prefill: mean latency 66ms, p95 150ms, p99 180ms, tokens/sec 1760
- Adaptive-batching new heuristic (alpha=0.25): stable throughput +5% vs static batch size for short sequences, slight p99 increase (~8ms) under 95th perc CPU jitter.

Kernel work notes
- PR 879: fused GEMM micro-optimizations (A->B transpose elimination on common shapes).
  - Observed: consistent throughput gains for sequence lengths < 2048.
  - Regression: occasional allocator fragmentation leading to OOM in long-context runs. Likely due to delayed free ordering when fused path triggers different intermediate buffers.
- PR 882: refactor of KV cache copy path to reduce memcpy for prefill. Still in review; bench shows 12% lower CPU overhead on host side.
- Next: land guarded allocations + leak detector patch (branch: leak-detect/alloc-guard). Need to run canary with long-run (>2 hour) synthetic traces.

KV cache / prefill experiments
- Goal: reduce repeated compute for prompt prefixes that map to same cache keys across requests (chatty apps with identical system prompts).
- Approach:
  - Prefill cache stores computed KV slices keyed by (model, version, prefix-hash, device-shard).
  - Coalescing: short-lived request bundling within window to share in-flight prefill builds.
- Observations this week:
  - Prefill key TTL of 60s hits best for demo traffic patterns; longer TTL increases memory pressure without proportional hit gains.
  - Eviction policy change: LRU + small-frequency boost for keys observed in the last 3 minutes; reduces thrash for background batch jobs.
  - Prefill compression: storing reduced-precision KV slices (float16->int8 quantization) saves 2x mem, cost is ~4ms extra expand on hit; total still net-positive for p99 in most flows.

Batching & coalescing notes
- Coalescing window tuned to 8ms for low-latency tier. Rationale: tradeoff between added latency for first request vs aggregation benefits.
- When combined with prefill: coalescing improves amortized kernel launch overhead dramatically for small token generation (<64 tokens).
- Adaptive batch sizing: prototype heuristic adjusts max batch size by observing queue depth and recent p99. Works well under stable load; oscillates under bursty spikes — need damping (suggested tau parameter).

CI / infra / flaky tests
- Flaky bun tests increased correlation with PR 879; reproducer added in infra/ci/longseq-repro. Run full mem-pressure suite nightly until allocation bug fixed.
- Load test harness: added a prefill-heavy scenario (emulates 60% prefilling, 20% identical prefixes). Results posted to linked artifacts.

Customer impact and rollout plan
- Do NOT enable fused GEMM path on Hosted canary until OOM fix confirmed. Risk: long-prompt customers (research notebooks) could see failures.
- Prefill + coalescing safe to enable on low-latency canary group (internal beta) — +p99 reduction observed and memory usage within tolerance when TTL=60s.
- Suggested canary phases:
  1) internal beta (small fleet, 24h) — prefill+coalesce only (no fused GEMM)
  2) expand to 10% of low-latency tier with guarded fused GEMM and leak detector enabled
  3) monitor for 72h, roll back on >0.05% error increase or any OOMs.

Open questions / items to investigate
- Root cause of allocator fragmentation with fused path: cuda mem pooling vs our allocator interplay? Ask infra/sre for trace from canary host where OOM occurred.
- Is the prefill key fingerprinting stable across quantized model variants? Need cross-variant hash compatibility tests.
- How to improve coalescing fairness: small high-priority requests should not be delayed — maybe priority bypass window.

Action items (owners)
- Aditi: run 48h canary with prefill+coalesce internal fleet (start 2026-04-15).
- Marcus: add deterministic repro for long-seq OOM and wire mem-trace (target 2026-04-14).
- Sofia: complete PR 882 review and add integration tests for prefill-quantized expansion (target 2026-04-16).
- Ethan: tune adaptive-batching damping param and run replay tests for bursty traffic (target 2026-04-18).

Notes to self
- Keep a tight watch on p99 and error-rate; small perf wins not worth customer-visible OOMs.
- Save baseline traces for postmortem if canary shows issues — include full kernel timeline.
